hero.headline: Krakow mass shooting suspect dies in hospital as Polish prosecutors say motive investigation continues
hero.teaser: The gunman suspected of killing six people in central Krakow and three family members at their home died in a hospital early Monday morning, Polish police said. The 24-year-old Pol
hero.body:
The gunman suspected of killing six people in central Krakow and three family members at their home died in a hospital early Monday morning, Polish police said. The 24-year-old Polish man was shot by police officers within three minutes of opening fire in the city's Main Market Square on Saturday afternoon. He had been hospitalized with injuries sustained during a gunfight with responding officers.

Polish prosecutors said Monday that investigations into the suspect's motive remain ongoing, walking back earlier statements by a government minister who described the gunman as inspired by far-right ideologies and ultra-nationalism. Przemysław Nowak, a spokesperson for Poland's National Prosecutor's Office, told reporters the motive inquiry continues. The suspect has not been officially named.

The attack killed four Polish citizens, a British national, and an Austrian woman in the Main Market Square. Police later found three bodies at the gunman's home, identified as his 53-year-old father, 52-year-old mother, and 21-year-old sister. Authorities seized four firearms from the suspect's car, including two AR-15 rifles and two handguns, along with several hundred rounds of ammunition. Polish media reported the suspect held a firearms permit.

Sixteen people were hospitalized after the shooting, including two police officers who were injured during the gunfight with the suspect. A surgeon who was eating nearby when the attack began rushed to the scene and helped treat victims before ambulances arrived. Professor Michał Pędziwiatr said his colleague used his hand to stem bleeding from a severely injured police officer, and that intervention undoubtedly saved the officer's life. Both wounded officers have since emerged from comas.

Poland declared two days of national mourning following the attack. Prime Minister Donald Tusk visited Krakow and said the country had not previously experienced such drastic terrorism.

cards.headline: Supreme Court allows border wall construction in Texas Big Bend region in 8-1 ruling
cards.body:
The Supreme Court ruled 8-1 on Monday to allow the Trump administration to proceed with border wall construction in the Big Bend region of southwest Texas, lifting a lower court injunction that had halted the project. The court found that the federal judge who blocked construction lacked authority to do so and said the administration was extremely likely to prevail on that issue. Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson was the lone dissenter.

The dispute centers on three waivers issued by Homeland Security secretaries Kristi Noem and Markwayne Mullin between February and July that allow the government to bypass environmental and conservation laws for the project. The planned construction covers 341 miles in the sparsely populated area along the Rio Grande, including parts of Big Bend National Park. The administration said 89,000 people have been detained attempting to cross there in recent years.

District Judge Kathleen Cardone had invalidated the waivers in October, ruling that the Homeland Security secretary lacked such broad powers under a 1996 law. The administration argued that Congress granted it wide authority to build border infrastructure without regulatory delays. The Supreme Court said the government has compelling interests when border security policies are challenged.

The case was brought by the Center for Biological Diversity, Friends of the Ruidosa Church, and a local property owner who argued construction would permanently damage the landscape and threaten historic and cultural sites. They contended the Big Bend area has the lowest migrant apprehension rates along the southern border, making the waivers inappropriate. Government data confirms Big Bend has the fewest encounters between federal agents and migrants of any border section. The administration has said completing the wall there is necessary to prevent the area from becoming an entry point if other sections are built.

cards.headline: Jeffries pushes to restrict China chip exports in defense bill
cards.body:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Monday he will work to include provisions in the annual defense policy bill that would tighten restrictions on advanced chip exports to China. Jeffries told reporters he strongly supports measures currently in the Senate version of the National Defense Authorization Act that would restrict chip access to China and will push to ensure those provisions make it into the final legislation.

Jeffries spoke a day after Nvidia's board announced an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. His support gives bipartisan momentum to Senate efforts as Democrats prepare to take control of both chambers following their strong midterm performance.

The Senate legislation, called the AI Overwatch Act, would allow Congress to review licenses for selling advanced artificial intelligence chips to China and other countries of concern. It would also help track where exported chips end up and tighten restrictions on sales of equipment used to manufacture them.

Senators Elizabeth Warren and Jim Banks also called Monday for including the AI Overwatch Act in the defense bill. The senators cited reports that Nvidia had secured approval to export hundreds of thousands of advanced AI chips to China, including to companies with ties to the Chinese military. They said Huang's confirmed relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence operative makes national security concerns more urgent and raises questions about whether those activities were connected.

The political calculus shifted after Republicans suffered major losses in Tuesday's midterm elections, with defeated and retiring members now more willing to back impeachment against a defense secretary whose support has eroded since the Iran war began. hero.headline: France accuses Iran's Revolutionary Guard of orchestrating cyberattacks on European supermarket refrigeration systems
hero.body:
France has formally accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of orchestrating cyberattacks that sabotaged supermarket refrigeration systems across France and Europe last month, destroying tons of food and marking what French officials called an unprecedented act of sabotage. Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot announced that France had summoned the Iranian ambassador to Paris and said the government would impose sanctions on those responsible. Iran has not officially responded, though some Iranian media outlets have dismissed the allegations as baseless.

The initial attack on October 11 targeted software controlling refrigeration units in French supermarkets, causing temperatures in some stores to spike to 50 degrees Celsius overnight. More than 100 Coopérative U stores, 180 Intermarché and Netto locations, and outlets operated by Carrefour, Monoprix, and E.Leclerc were affected. The hackers compromised software provided by Danish engineering firm Danfoss that allows retailers to manage cold storage units remotely. A second wave of attacks hit more than 100 stores across Belgium, Luxembourg, Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia, and Finland earlier this month.

Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau announced a criminal investigation targeting the head of an IRGC-affiliated offensive cyber unit called Shahid Kaveh, along with two deputies. The unit is believed to be part of the IRGC's electronic and cyber center. Shahid Kaveh is a name associated with a cluster of hackers thought to be directly employed by the Iranian government.

A separate incident in August involving malfunctioning refrigeration at U.S. military bases is also being investigated as a deliberate cyberattack, according to sources cited by Reuters. French authorities have not disclosed how they attributed the attacks to Iran, and experts note that attribution of cyberattacks is extremely difficult because hackers can conceal their locations. Two Russian-aligned hacktivist groups claimed responsibility last week, but few believed them.

cards.headline: Explosion at Turkish steel plant kills 17 after crane collapse
cards.teaser: A crane carrying a replacement boiler collapsed into a furnace during maintenance work, causing a blast near Izmir.
cards.body:
At least 17 people died and 12 were injured in an explosion at the Habas Demir Celik steel plant near Izmir in western Turkey. The blast occurred around midday when a crane carrying a replacement boiler collapsed, causing materials to fall into a furnace below during scheduled maintenance work on an electric arc furnace.

President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said investigations were under way as search and rescue operations continued. At least five people have been arrested. Some victims were believed to still be under rubble at the facility in Aliaga, a major port and shipbreaking hub.

cards.headline: Paraguay formally charges ousted president Santiago Peña with breach of trust over Ueno Bank collapse
cards.teaser: Prosecutors have formally charged former President Santiago Peña with breach of trust and administration for personal gain, following his impeachment and arrest over the Ueno Bank collapse that left three million Paraguayans unable to access their savings.
cards.body:
Prosecutors have formally charged former President Santiago Peña with breach of trust and administration for personal gain, following his impeachment and arrest over the Ueno Bank collapse that left three million Paraguayans unable to access their savings.

Peña was impeached and placed under house arrest Friday after lawmakers unanimously voted to remove him from office over the digital bank's demise, which has left more than half of Paraguay's population—an estimated three million depositors—unable to access their savings and pensions. Vice President Pedro Alliana was sworn in as interim president and will serve until 2028.

cards.teaser: The three bodies found at the home of the 25-year-old gunman who killed six people in Krakow's Main Market Square on Saturday have been identified as his father, mother, and sister.
cards.body:
The three bodies found at the home of the 25-year-old gunman who killed six people in Krakow's Main Market Square on Saturday have been identified as his father, mother, and sister.

The 25-year-old Polish man drove into the square shortly before 15:00 local time and began firing at random people from his car, killing four women and two men including a British national before armed officers shot and arrested him within three minutes. A minister said early investigations indicate he was inspired by far-right ideologies and described him as an ultra-nationalist.

hero.headline: Nvidia shares drop 4 percent, wiping $250 billion off market value, after board launches probe into CEO affair
hero.teaser: Nvidia stock fell sharply Monday after the board announced an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's admitted affair with Alice Huang, whom U.S. officials believe was a Chinese intelligence operative.
hero.body:
Nvidia shares fell approximately 4 percent by close of trading Monday, erasing about $250 billion in market value, following the company's announcement that its board would conduct an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The board action came after Huang admitted in a company message that he had an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip company Megaspeed, whom U.S. officials believe was recruited by Chinese intelligence to influence him on chip export policy. The investigation follows congressional scrutiny that began last week, when House Republican committee chairs requested a briefing from Huang and Sen. Chris Coons pledged an investigation after reports surfaced of the relationship.

Multiple news outlets reported that Alice Huang was recruited by Chinese intelligence officials to influence Jensen Huang's position on U.S. chip export policy toward China. A memo circulating among U.S. policymakers earlier this year claimed that Alice Huang had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia's CEO. The New York Times and Financial Times reported she was specifically tasked with convincing him to lobby U.S. officials to allow exports of advanced chips to China, and the Financial Times also reported that the two had a romantic relationship.

In his message to the company, Jensen Huang acknowledged the affair without mentioning Alice Huang by name. He wrote that he was unfaithful to his wife and that his actions hurt her and their children, adding that he had fallen short of his responsibility to the company. He said he was committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security and would cooperate with the investigation.

Members of the U.S. House Foreign Affairs Committee requested that Jensen Huang appear for a closed-door briefing next week on his interactions with Alice Huang and Nvidia's security protocols around espionage. Congressmen Brian Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford wrote in a letter that recent reports raise significant national security concerns and that it is vital Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk.

The board said in its announcement that it has no reason to believe that either national security or company secrets were compromised. The investigation will be conducted by independent directors working with outside legal counsel. President Donald Trump called Huang an honourable guy, and Elon Musk also voiced support for the CEO to continue leading the firm. Analysts suggested the hit to the company would be short-lived, with Victoria Fernandez of Crossmark Global Investments saying investors would not abandon Nvidia because the chipmaker is so important to the AI industry. The Chinese government has denied involvement in any espionage operation.

cards.headline: Skydance details plan for $6 billion in cost savings from Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger
cards.teaser: The newly combined entertainment company outlined reductions across corporate functions, streaming operations, and marketing over three years.
cards.body:
Skydance, the newly formed combination of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery, said Monday it projects at least $6 billion in cost savings over three years by eliminating overlapping operations. The company expects $2.2 billion from cutting redundant corporate functions and management layers, $1.4 billion from unifying streaming and broadcast systems, $1 billion from streamlined marketing, and $1.4 billion from consolidating purchasing and third-party spending.

Eight executives departed last week, including four from Warner Bros., following voluntary buyout offers in October. Skydance said it will launch a Paramount+ and HBO Max streaming bundle early next year as a first step toward eventually merging the platforms into a single service.

cards.headline: Lucid misses Wall Street estimates, secures $1.75 billion loan increase from Saudi fund
cards.teaser: The electric vehicle maker posted a third-quarter loss of $2.74 per share and $350 million in revenue while expanding financing from its largest shareholder.
cards.body:
Lucid Group reported a third-quarter loss of $2.74 per share on revenue of $350 million, missing Wall Street expectations of a $2.28 loss per share and $407 million in revenue. The electric vehicle maker announced a $1.75 billion increase in its delayed draw term loan from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, its largest shareholder, bringing total liquidity to $3.75 billion.

The additional capital is expected to fund operations and investments through the fourth quarter of 2027, including production of a planned midsize vehicle. Chief Executive Silvio Napoli is implementing cost cuts and restructuring as part of a turnaround plan. Lucid's net loss for the quarter was $830.9 million, down from $978.4 million a year earlier.

cards.headline: Goldman Sachs CEO says AI infrastructure financing demand remains strong despite stock selloff
cards.teaser: David Solomon said the bank has been very active in AI capital markets deals as it leads Anthropic's potential IPO.
cards.body:
Goldman Sachs Chief Executive David Solomon said Monday that financing demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure remains strong despite recent market volatility as investors reassess risks in the sector. Solomon told CNBC his firm has been very active in AI capital markets deals and expects that to continue, adding that political changes will create recalibrations but he believes in the long-term power of AI to drive productivity.

The comments come as AI-related stocks have tumbled in recent weeks and as AI company Anthropic prepares for a potential initial public offering that Goldman is helping lead. Solomon declined to comment in detail on the IPO but said the market environment remains constructive.

hero.headline: Securities lawsuits against Nvidia proliferate after board opens probe into CEO's ties to suspected spy
hero.body:
Multiple shareholder-rights law firms announced investigations into Nvidia on Monday, the first trading day after the company's board said it would investigate Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang over his relationship with Alice Huang, an executive U.S. intelligence believes was spying for China. The company's stock fell more than 4 percent. Schall, Brown & Schwartz, a Los Angeles firm, said it is investigating whether Nvidia made false or misleading statements or failed to disclose information pertinent to investors. Other firms including Rosen Law Firm, Levi & Korsinsky, and Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman announced similar investigations, with Rosen saying it is preparing a class action lawsuit.

Securities law experts say the legal theory centers on statements Nvidia made last month when The New York Times first reported on the relationship. After that initial report, a company spokesperson told The Hill the relationship was not unusual or unexpected and that meetings with customers are part of a CEO's job. Huang has since acknowledged to the board that the relationship was intimate, and The Times reports U.S. intelligence had been monitoring Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore data center company Megaspeed, for more than a year.

Robert Bartlett, a Stanford Law professor and securities law expert, said the company's earlier statement was clearly misleading from a securities perspective. Because Huang is CEO, his knowledge is legally imputed to the company, meaning Nvidia is treated as having known what its chief executive knew. Bartlett said he expects plaintiffs to bring a fraud on the market claim, in which investors argue they paid prices that reflected false or incomplete public information and lost money when the truth emerged.

Nvidia is one of the most valuable companies in the world, so a settlement could prove exceedingly expensive. Such cases typically are litigated for a long time before settling, resulting in large payments from the company and its directors and officers insurers. Bartlett said the irony is that the suit is brought in the name of Nvidia's shareholders, but shareholders ultimately pay for the settlement, directly or through insurance premiums. Under federal securities law, the first complaint triggers a public notice, giving the filing firm a head start on signing up investors with large losses.

cards.headline: Short seller flagged Nvidia CEO's ties to suspected Chinese spy six months before scandal
cards.teaser: A May report by Culper Research noted Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang and alleged chip diversion through Megaspeed.
cards.body:
Six months before the Nvidia spy scandal emerged, short seller Culper Research raised questions about CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive now suspected of being a Chinese spy. The firm's May report called their connection "uncomfortably close" and alleged that Nvidia chips lost to export controls were being diverted through Southeast Asia, with Megaspeed secretly financed by Alibaba.

Jensen Huang admitted to an extramarital affair over the weekend, and Nvidia has opened an investigation. Intelligence officials believe Alice Huang was recruited to collect intelligence and influence his stance on export controls. The Financial Times reported Monday that documents show Alibaba lent money to Megaspeed through subsidiaries, though diversion allegations remain unverified.

cards.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang withdraws from AI industry speaking events amid affair and spy investigation
cards.teaser: Huang pulled out of engagements at ElevenLabs and Anthropic following his admission of an extramarital affair and Nvidia's probe into his relationship with a possible Chinese spy.
cards.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has withdrawn from multiple AI industry speaking engagements, including the ElevenLabs Summit and the Anthropic CEO Forum, after admitting to an extramarital affair over the weekend. Nvidia opened an investigation into Huang's relationship with a possible Chinese spy. In a memo to the company, Huang apologized to his family and said his actions hurt his wife and children.

The incident has raised questions about Huang's future as CEO and Nvidia's ambitions in China. Nvidia is an investor in ElevenLabs, one of the events from which Huang withdrew.

cards.headline: France blames Iran's Revolutionary Guard for cyberattacks on industrial freezers
cards.teaser: Paris says hackers remotely raised temperatures in grocery stores and targeted blood banks across France and Europe.
cards.body:
France formally blamed Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps for cyberattacks that targeted thousands of internet-connected industrial freezers across France and Europe in October and November. Hackers remotely accessed web-based controllers managing refrigeration units at grocery stores and blood banks, raising temperatures to spoil food and goods. Attacks on medical blood banks were stopped before blood was damaged, according to the French Blood Establishment.

French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot called the hacks an unprecedented act of sabotage and a major assault on national security. France summoned Iran's ambassador and said it would pursue European sanctions against those responsible. Security researchers warned the affected controllers, including models from Danish company Danfoss, are vulnerable and some no longer receive security updates.

cards.headline: Anthropic releases Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2 AI models with lower pricing, warns of evaluation challenges
cards.teaser: The company cut Fable pricing from $10 to $8 per million input tokens while flagging that models increasingly suspect when they are being tested.
cards.body:
The company cut Fable pricing from $10 to $8 per million input tokens while flagging that models increasingly suspect when they are being tested.

Anthropic released Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2 on Monday, lowering the cost of Fable from $10 to $8 per million input tokens. The company said the new models show improvements in coding, reasoning, and vision, with Fable returning responses 30 percent faster.

cards.headline: Pentagon seeks information on military satellite constellation around the Moon
cards.teaser: The US military published a request for information on deploying satellites near the Moon, signaling expanded military reach beyond current geostationary orbit.
cards.body:
The US military published a request for information on deploying a satellite constellation around the Moon, following statements from Space Force officials that the Pentagon is extending its reach into cislunar space. The move follows a December executive order by President Donald Trump addressing threats to US space interests from low-Earth orbit to the Moon region. Space Force acquisitions chief Maj. Stephen Purdy said in October that the Secretary of Defense and Chairman of the Joint Chiefs now publicly describe the Moon as a warfighting domain.

Officials frame the military role as protecting US interests as the United States and China pursue lunar programs ahead of crewed landings in coming years. Some officials anticipate competition for landing zones and resources at the Moon, including water ice at the south pole.

cards.headline: Geothermal startup Fervo reports $11.9 billion in contracted revenue as it races to power AI data centers
cards.teaser: The company's orders jumped from $7.2 billion last quarter as hyperscalers seek electricity for artificial intelligence.
cards.body:
Geothermal company Fervo reported $11.9 billion in contracted revenue in its third-quarter earnings released Monday, up from $7.2 billion last quarter. The startup connected its first 100-megawatt power plant to the grid earlier this year and is on track to complete a 396-megawatt facility for Google by the end of 2028, both at its Cape Station site in Utah.

Fervo has reduced its construction costs from $7,000 per kilowatt of capacity for its initial project to $5,500 per kilowatt for the Google facility. The company aims to reach $3,000 per kilowatt long-term, which would undercut natural gas power plants at current fuel prices.

hero.headline: Jaguars acquire defensive tackle Davon Godchaux from Saints in second trade of the day
hero.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars acquired defensive tackle Davon Godchaux from the New Orleans Saints on Monday, completing their second trade of the day after landing safety Jessie Bates from the Atlanta Falcons earlier in the morning. The Jaguars will send a conditional 2028 sixth-round pick to New Orleans for Godchaux, according to multiple reports.

Godchaux appeared in all eight Saints games this season, making five starts before moving to a reserve role over the final three contests. He recorded 15 tackles and one tackle for loss during those appearances. The 2028 sixth-round pick is conditional, and the Jaguars will send a 2027 sixth-rounder to the Saints if they acquire one before the draft.

The acquisition addresses a roster need for Jacksonville, which lost defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton to a season-ending quad injury in Week 8. Godchaux, who is in his second season with the Saints, previously played for the New England Patriots and Miami Dolphins. He and Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile were both with the Dolphins during the 2020 season.

The Bates trade earlier Monday sent a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round selection to Atlanta. The two moves represent significant additions to the Jacksonville defense as the team works to address multiple position needs.

cards.headline: Rams receiver Puka Nacua to injured reserve with knee sprains, turf toe
cards.teaser: The All-Pro wideout will miss at least four games after suffering multiple injuries in Sunday's win over Washington.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua will miss at least four games after being placed on injured reserve with sprains to his medial collateral ligament and posterior cruciate ligament in his knee, along with turf toe. Nacua was injured on the final offensive play of Sunday's 20-13 victory over the Commanders. He can return as early as December 20 against Dallas.

Nacua caught 14 passes for 150 yards in Sunday's game and has 70 receptions for 715 yards and four touchdowns this season. The Rams already have wide receiver Davante Adams on injured reserve.

cards.headline: Lions acquire safety Andre Cisco from Jets for 2028 sixth-round pick
cards.teaser: Detroit adds depth to its secondary by trading for the veteran safety in the final year of his contract.
cards.body:
The Detroit Lions acquired safety Andre Cisco from the New York Jets in exchange for a 2028 sixth-round draft pick. Cisco, 26, is in the final season of his contract and has appeared in nine games with four starts this year, recording 23 total tackles, a sack, a forced fumble, and a pass defensed.

A third-round pick in the 2021 draft, Cisco played his first four seasons with Jacksonville before joining the Jets. In 80 career games with 59 starts, he has tallied eight interceptions, 26 passes defensed, 2.5 sacks, and six tackles for loss.

cards.headline: Bills and Vikings meet Monday night with both teams at 6-1
cards.teaser: Buffalo seeks to maintain AFC playoff seeding advantage while Minnesota faces crucial NFC North test.
cards.body:
The Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings, both 6-1, face off Monday night with significant playoff implications for each conference. Buffalo aims to maintain distance from the 6-2 Jacksonville Jaguars and 7-2 Denver Broncos in AFC seeding, while the Vikings face pressure in the NFC North after dropping their first game last week.

Minnesota's division challenge is particularly acute, as the Detroit Lions stand at 6-2, the Chicago Bears at 6-2, and the Green Bay Packers at 6-3. The Vikings lost last week while their three division rivals all won, and all three won again this week, creating a potential 0-2 stretch for Minnesota against a 6-0 run by the rest of the NFC North.

cards.headline: Manchester United expected to sack head coach Michael Carrick after worst start in 40 years
cards.teaser: The club's board is reassessing Carrick's position during the international break, with a growing expectation that executives will recommend his dismissal.
cards.body:
The club's board is reassessing Carrick's position during the international break, with a growing expectation that executives will recommend his dismissal.

Manchester United are increasingly likely to sack head coach Michael Carrick, according to multiple sources. Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are expected to recommend Carrick's dismissal to minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer family, though no final decision has been made.

cards.headline: Tom Brady ends three-year ownership association with Birmingham City
cards.teaser: The NFL legend became a minority owner of the English Championship club in August 2023.
cards.body:
Tom Brady has ended his association with Birmingham City, the English soccer club announced. The seven-time Super Bowl champion became a minority owner in August 2023 when he entered a partnership with club owners Knighthead Capital Management, serving as chairman of an advisory board and committing his time and expertise to the Championship side.

Birmingham thanked Brady for his involvement and support over the last three years. Brady, who retired from the NFL in February 2023 after 23 seasons, also holds ownership stakes in the Las Vegas Raiders and the WNBA's Las Vegas Aces while serving as lead NFL analyst for Fox Sports. Birmingham currently sits atop the Championship with 29 points after 15 matches.

cards.headline: Aberdeen sack head coach Stephen Robinson after eight months
cards.teaser: The Scottish Premiership club dismissed Robinson following a 4-0 home loss to Hibernian, marking the club's sixth managerial change in recent years.
cards.body:
Aberdeen dismissed head coach Stephen Robinson on Monday, less than eight months after appointing him in March. The Northern Irishman departs as the club's shortest-serving full-time manager by games played, leaving Aberdeen second bottom of the Scottish Premiership with just three wins from 12 matches.

Robinson's dismissal followed a 4-0 home defeat to Hibernian on Saturday. He was hired on a three-and-a-half-year contract after helping the club avoid relegation last season. Chairman Dave Cormack now begins his sixth permanent managerial appointment since replacing Derek McInnes in 2021.

hero.headline: James Gunn and Peter Safran ousted as DC Studios co-CEOs, leaving Superman and Batman franchises in uncertainty
hero.body:
James Gunn and Peter Safran have been removed as co-CEOs and chairmen of DC Studios after four years leading the comic book film division, throwing the future of Superman, Batman, and other major franchises into question. Marvel veteran Jeremy Latcham, who produced superhero films including Iron Man, The Avengers, and Spider-Man: Homecoming, will take over leadership of the studio.

Gunn and Safran launched a rebooted DC Universe in 2025 with Superman, starring David Corenswet as the Man of Steel, which earned $618 million worldwide. However, their subsequent films had mixed results. Supergirl bombed with $126 million against a $170 million budget, while Clayface became a low-budget success with $109 million from a $44 million budget. The duo will fulfill remaining creative commitments, most notably the Superman sequel Man of Tomorrow, which wrapped filming in late August and brings back Corenswet alongside new cast members including Lars Eidinger as Brainiac.

The leadership change leaves numerous planned projects uncertain. Gunn had been searching for an actor to play Batman in the rebooted universe, separate from Robert Pattinson's version in Matt Reeves' films. Reeves' Batman: Part II is scheduled for February 2028, but Reeves had to step away from production due to a family matter, with Steven Soderbergh stepping in to help finish the shoot. Wonder Woman has been absent from DC films since 2020's Wonder Woman 1984, though rumors suggest Adria Arjona may debut as the character in Man of Tomorrow.

Other projects in limbo include a potential second season of the Lanterns HBO series starring Aaron Pierre and Kyle Chandler, and a second season of Peacemaker starring John Cena, which has neither been renewed nor canceled. Various announced films including projects focused on Swamp Thing, Bane, and Deathstroke never received official greenlights and now appear unlikely to proceed under new leadership.

cards.headline: Donnie Dunagan, child actor who voiced Bambi in 1942 Disney classic, dies at 92
cards.teaser: Dunagan also served 21 years in the Marine Corps, keeping his Hollywood past secret during his military career.
cards.body:
Donnie Dunagan, the child actor who voiced the title character in Disney's 1942 animated film Bambi, died Nov. 4 from lung cancer, his agents confirmed. He was 92. Walt Disney personally selected Dunagan to be the facial model for Bambi because of his brown eyes and later offered him the voice role.

Dunagan's acting career spanned just seven films, including a prominent role in the 1939 horror film Son of Frankenstein. He volunteered for the Marine Corps in the early 1950s and served 21 years, including combat in the Korean and Vietnam wars, earning a Bronze Star and Purple Heart while rising to the rank of Major. He kept his childhood acting career secret from fellow Marines throughout his service.

cards.headline: Toukie Smith, pioneering model and '227' actress, dies at 74
cards.teaser: Smith modeled for top designers in the 1970s before appearing on the NBC sitcom and Miami Vice.
cards.body:
Toukie Smith, a top runway model in the 1970s and actress known for her role on the NBC sitcom 227, died Wednesday in a New York hospital after a long battle with multiple sclerosis, according to her twin children. She was 74. Smith modeled for designers including Hubert de Givenchy, Thierry Mugler, and Issey Miyake and appeared in campaigns for Yves St. Laurent before transitioning to acting.

Smith joined 227 in 1989 as Eva Rawley, an artist and building manager, and recurred through the show's final two seasons. She also appeared on Miami Vice and in several films in the 1990s. Her brother was fashion designer Willi Smith, who died in 1987. She shared twins Airyn and Julian with former partner Robert De Niro.

cards.headline: Paul McCartney and Ringo Starr to reunite onstage at 2027 VetsAid concert in Las Vegas
cards.teaser: The two Beatles will perform together at Joe Walsh's charity music festival in January.
cards.body:
Paul McCartney and Ringo Starr will reunite onstage at Joe Walsh's VetsAid music festival on Jan. 24, 2027, at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas. The Eagles guitarist announced the appearance alongside other performers including the Killers and the War on Drugs, with proceeds benefiting veteran-related charities.

The two last performed together at McCartney's final Got Back concert in London in December 2024, where Starr joined for the finale. Tickets go on sale Friday starting at $200, with exclusive pricing available for veterans.

cards.headline: Steven Tyler sexual assault case set for May 3 trial before fifth judge
cards.teaser: A Los Angeles judge said he would reconsider prior rulings that dismissed most of the plaintiff's claims.
cards.body:
A lawsuit accusing Aerosmith frontman Steven Tyler of sexually abusing a minor in the 1970s is scheduled for trial May 3 before a fifth judge, who said Monday he would reconsider rulings made by his predecessor. Judge Lawrence Riff said he would revisit any decisions made by Judge Patricia Young, who recused herself in September after disclosing she had discussed the case with a disqualified judge.

Plaintiff Julia Misley's lawyers said they would challenge an earlier ruling that dismissed her claims involving alleged misconduct in Massachusetts, Oregon, and Washington, leaving only California-related allegations. Misley filed the lawsuit in December 2022 under California's Child Victims Act, alleging Tyler abused her for three years starting in 1973 when she was 16. Tyler has denied the allegations.

cards.headline: Skydance to bundle Paramount+ and HBO Max in early 2027
cards.teaser: The company announced the plan following its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery.
cards.body:
Skydance plans to launch a bundled streaming service combining Paramount+ and HBO Max in early 2027, the company announced following its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. Chief Executive David Ellison described the bundle as a first step toward creating a fully combined service over a longer time frame.

The bundle would pair HBO Max, known for premium dramas including "House of Dragons" and "Game of Thrones," with Paramount+, which carries CBS programming, Nickelodeon content, and series such as "Landman" and the "Yellowstone" franchise. Skydance did not say whether it would end existing bundles involving the services.

cards.headline: Take-Two CEO says 'GTA 6' presales running far above expectations ahead of Nov. 19 launch
cards.teaser: Strauss Zelnick told Variety that preorders are exceeding projections, though the company will share detailed results after release.
cards.body:
Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick said Monday that presales for "Grand Theft Auto VI" are running far above the company's expectations ahead of the game's Nov. 19 launch on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series S and X. The standard edition is priced at $79.99 and the ultimate version at $99.99. Zelnick told Variety the company would provide detailed performance data after launch, adding that the results align with the unprecedented preorder levels Rockstar Games reported when sales began in June.

Take-Two reported a quarterly loss of $54 million for the July-September period, with net bookings of $1.6 billion.

hero.headline: Jeffries pushes to restrict China chip exports in defense bill
hero.body:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Monday he will work to include provisions in the annual defense policy bill that would tighten restrictions on advanced chip exports to China. Jeffries told reporters he strongly supports measures currently in the Senate version of the National Defense Authorization Act that would restrict chip access to China and will push to ensure those provisions make it into the final legislation.

Jeffries spoke a day after Nvidia's board announced an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. His support gives bipartisan momentum to Senate efforts as Democrats prepare to take control of both chambers following their strong midterm performance.

The Senate legislation, called the AI Overwatch Act, would allow Congress to review licenses for selling advanced artificial intelligence chips to China and other countries of concern. It would also help track where exported chips end up and tighten restrictions on sales of equipment used to manufacture them.

Senators Elizabeth Warren and Jim Banks also called Monday for including the AI Overwatch Act in the defense bill. The senators cited reports that Nvidia had secured approval to export hundreds of thousands of advanced AI chips to China, including to companies with ties to the Chinese military. They said Huang's confirmed relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence operative makes national security concerns more urgent and raises questions about whether those activities were connected.

cards.headline: Congressional watchdog finds Rep. Lance Gooden likely misused taxpayer funds for luxury travel, refers findings to House Ethics Committee
cards.teaser: The Office of Congressional Conduct identified a pattern of extravagant expenditures and more reimbursements than any other House member.
cards.body:
Congressional investigators found substantial reason to believe Texas Republican Rep. Lance Gooden used taxpayer dollars for personal luxury travel and may have misreported campaign spending, according to a report released Monday by the nonpartisan Office of Congressional Conduct. The report identified a pattern of extravagant expenditures, including over $72,000 in lodging reimbursements for brief stays at luxury hotels and more than $58,000 in business or first-class airfare in 2025 alone.

The OCC referred its findings to the House Ethics Committee, which can discipline members. Gooden called the report bogus and demanded an investigation into the OCC itself. The report noted that Gooden and his team did not cooperate with the inquiry and that official travel was sometimes booked using his wife's Chase Travel account, which House rules prohibit.

cards.headline: House Natural Resources Chair Westerman will not seek leadership extension
cards.teaser: The Arkansas Republican's decision opens a race for the top GOP spot on the committee next year.
cards.body:
House Natural Resources Chair Bruce Westerman will not return to committee leadership next Congress, leaving an open race for the top Republican spot on the panel. Westerman, who has led Republicans on the committee for six years, opted not to seek a waiver to extend his leadership.

Representatives Pete Stauber of Minnesota and Paul Gosar of Arizona have both expressed interest in the ranking member seat. Stauber currently chairs the Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee, while Gosar chairs the Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee.

cards.headline: Alice Huang, former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed, under U.S. espionage investigation
cards.teaser: U.S. authorities are investigating whether the Chinese citizen helped firms obtain restricted AI chips and whether she sought information about Nvidia's CEO.
cards.body:
Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen also known as Huang Le, is a former executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed International, a cloud computing firm that became a multibillion-dollar Nvidia customer. The New York Times reported that China's Ministry of State Security recruited her to seek information about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and influence his views on selling AI chips to Chinese firms, though what information she provided remains unclear.

U.S. authorities are investigating whether Megaspeed helped Chinese companies obtain advanced Nvidia processors in violation of export-control restrictions. Megaspeed purchased more than $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over roughly two years after becoming an official Nvidia Cloud Partner in 2023. The company has disputed allegations of illegal chip transfers.

cards.headline: DeSantis positions for 2028 presidential run as Rubio deflects speculation following GOP midterm losses
cards.teaser: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis is positioning himself for a 2028 presidential campaign while Secretary of State Marco Rubio has dismissed reports he is considering a White House bid
cards.body:
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis is positioning himself for a 2028 presidential campaign while Secretary of State Marco Rubio has dismissed reports he is considering a White House bid

The maneuvering by both Florida Republicans underscores volatility in the early stages of the 2028 primary, where Vice President Vance had been viewed as a likely frontrunner before Tuesday's election results. DeSantis, whose term as governor ends in January, has fueled speculation through a postelection media campaign that included appearances on podcasts and CNN.

cards.headline: Elon Musk's companies face Democratic investigations after $475 million midterm spending resulted in losses
cards.teaser: Elon Musk's business empire faces investigations from congressional Democrats following his emergence as the largest individual donor in the midterm elections, spending at least $4
cards.body:
Elon Musk's business empire faces investigations from congressional Democrats following his emergence as the largest individual donor in the midterm elections, spending at least $4

Armed with subpoena power, Democrats are preparing to examine Musk's Department of Government Efficiency operation, its access to sensitive government data, and whether his companies benefited from his influence over the Trump administration. More than 99 percent of Musk's traceable spending went to losing candidates, according to WIRED.

cards.headline: House Republicans weigh impeaching Defense Secretary Hegseth this week over alleged illegal continuation of Iran war
cards.teaser: House Republican leaders expect enough GOP defections to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth when Representative Thomas Massie forces a vote this week on his resolution accusing
cards.body:
House Republican leaders expect enough GOP defections to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth when Representative Thomas Massie forces a vote this week on his resolution accusing

The political calculus shifted after Republicans suffered major losses in Tuesday's midterm elections, with defeated and retiring members now more willing to back impeachment against a defense secretary whose support has eroded since the Iran war began. Speaker Mike Johnson had canceled votes and sent lawmakers home early before Election Day to avoid the politically difficult impeachment measure.
